name: SoulWindowsCycle
source:
The windows to his soul were pried open wide 
 Stuck on death, chaos, confusion, fear, 
 Watching as the surrounding life and all he held dear 
 Would do nothing but continually steer 
 Him to a cycle of time that would not step aside. 
 
 Countless doors slamming into his face 
 As each blink recalls yet another key thrown 
 Into drowning silence, the locked and unknown 
 Now common, collected, forever sown 
 By a mind running a circular race. 
 
 A gentle caress does nothing to repair 
 Such battered hinges, broken frames, 
 Piled atop windowless sills etched with names 
 Of the lasting moments, those whose aims 
 Are to lock him away, with just enough air.
retelling:
Narrator: The silent observer, a detached entity confined within the labyrinth of the protagonist's mind, bearing witness to his tormented existence.

   In the vast expanse of time and space, there exists an eternal cycle, a circular race that entraps one soul - Him. This soul is trapped in a world that pulses with death, chaos, confusion, fear; a realm where his emotions and experiences are the landscape.

   From my vantage point, I see the countless doors slamming shut upon him, each slam echoing through the void, resonating with the rhythm of despair. The mind that houses him is in constant motion, running in circles like a ship lost at sea, seeking solace it cannot find.

   His attempts at escaping this maze are as futile as a bird attempting to break free from its cage. He reaches out for gentle caresses, but they offer only temporary relief before being swept away by the tide of fear and chaos once more.

   Beyond the veil of his mind, I sense a hostile reality that seems indifferent to his suffering. The external world is locked and unknown, symbolized by the windowless sills and just enough air to keep him alive but never truly free.

   Yet, amidst all this suffering, there remains a spark - a flicker of life. A testament to his resilience, a beacon in the darkness that speaks volumes about his indomitable spirit.

   Despite my role as an observer, I cannot help but feel a strange connection with him. For every door that slams shut, I am reminded of the unyielding nature of our existence. And for every circle he runs, I see a reminder of our shared human struggle against adversity.

   In the end, I remain here, observing, bearing witness to his plight. Will I ever understand his pain? Perhaps not. But perhaps it is enough for me to simply bear witness, to offer my silent support through the countless doors that slam shut upon him.
